post.description: Always 202 on a well-formed number — this never reveals whether an account already exists for that phone. Rate-limited per phone: a 60s cooldown between requests, and a 5-per-hour cap (see OTP_COOLDOWN / OTP_RATE_LIMITED below).

409.description: OTP_COOLDOWN (resend too soon) or OTP_RATE_LIMITED (5/hour exceeded).

post.description: Creates the User on first-ever verification for a phone number (passwordless signup and login are the same operation). On success, sets httpOnly cb_access_token and cb_refresh_token cookies AND returns the access token in the body — every endpoint accepts either the cookie or an Authorization: Bearer header, so a non-browser client can authenticate purely off this response with no cookie jar at all.

404.description: OTP_NOT_FOUND — no active (unexpired, unconsumed) code for this number.

409.description: OTP_INVALID (wrong code) or OTP_ATTEMPTS_EXCEEDED (5 wrong guesses — even the correct code is now rejected; request a new one).

post.summary: Verify an OTP and sign in

post.description: Body is optional and normally omitted — the refresh token is read from the cb_refresh_token cookie. Reusing an already-rotated token revokes the whole token family (REFRESH_REUSE_DETECTED), not just the presented token — this is the reuse-of-a-stolen-token detection. Returns a fresh access token in the body, same as /auth/otp/verify.
Revokes the refresh token family and clears both auth cookies.

Accepts the access token either as the cb_access_token cookie or an Authorization: Bearer header. Returns only the token's identity claims — id and phoneE164. For the owner's actual profile data (name, email, onboarding status, fields), use GET /profile/me instead; auth stays scoped to "who is this token for", not "what do we know about them".

401.description: UNAUTHENTICATED — missing, invalid, or expired token.

post.summary: Check whether the caller is signed in

get.description: identity + personal + work[] + business[] + socials[] + financial.* — the same shape POST /profile/onboarding accepts and returns. This is the read model for a profile screen; GET /profile/fields is the flat list used by the field editor.

post.description: One-shot — 409 if onboarding has already been completed. Only identity (firstName, lastName, primaryEmail) is required; every other section is optional and can be filled in later through the field and group endpoints instead. Do not send primaryPhone (it is your OTP-verified number, not a new input) or profilePhoto (use POST /profile/photo separately) — both are rejected as unknown properties by the request validator.

get.description: Ordered by position. Archived fields are excluded unless includeArchived=true.

post.description: BANK_ACCOUNT, DIGITAL_WALLET, and CRYPTO_WALLET values are encrypted at rest automatically — nothing to opt into. PHOTO cannot be created here; use POST /profile/photo.

patch.description: type is immutable — delete and recreate the field to change it.

delete.description: Soft delete — the field is archived, not hard-deleted, so any card history that referenced it stays displayable. Removing a PHOTO field also deletes its GCS object.

put.description: All-or-nothing: if any id does not belong to you, none are reordered.

get.description: Each group includes its own fields, already ordered — a job with its phone/email/title nested together, not a flat list you have to regroup client-side.

parameters.name: includeArchived
parameters.description: Include archived groups and their fields.

post.description: One instance of a repeatable thing — a specific job, business, bank account, or social profile. Add fields into it afterward via POST /profile/fields with this group's id.

patch.summary: Rename or recategorize a profile field group

delete.description: Archives the group AND every field in it — removing a job takes its phone/email/title with it, not just the job label.

post.description: JPEG, PNG, or WebP, up to 20 MB. Replacing an existing photo deletes the old one from storage.
post.summary: Upload or replace your profile photo

post.description: Upserts on (you, phoneE164) — calling this again for a number already in your registry updates displayName/notes rather than erroring. For adding many at once (e.g. a device address book), use POST /contacts/import instead.
post.summary: Add a contact, or update one that already exists

patch.description: phoneE164 is not editable here — it is the identity a contact is matched by.
patch.summary: Update a contact’s display name or notes

post.description: The expected way contacts actually enter the registry — hand over an address book export in one call instead of one POST /contacts per person. Each entry upserts the same way POST /contacts does; newly-created rows are tagged source=IMPORTED.

get.description: Archived cards are excluded unless includeArchived=true.

post.description: Starts with no fields — add them with PUT /cards/:id/fields. multipart/form-data, not JSON: the same call optionally accepts a logo file (field name `file`) alongside the card fields below, since a file and a JSON body cannot be mixed in one request. Omit `file` for a card with no logo — everything else works exactly the same. JPEG, PNG, or WebP, up to 20 MB; a card can also get (or replace) a logo later via POST /cards/:id/logo.

file.description: Optional logo — omit for no logo.

fieldIds.description: Profile field IDs to attach atomically on creation. All must belong to the caller; PHOTO fields are rejected.

get.description: Includes its curated field list, resolved and decrypted — the same view an edit screen would render.

patch.description: Any subset of the fields below. Omitted = leave alone; explicit `null` (on every nullable field) clears it back to unset. `coverUrl` is the one exception in the other direction — the only value it ever accepts is `null`, to remove the cover; a real cover can only be set via POST /cards/:id/cover.
patch.summary: Rename, recategorize, or restyle a card

delete.description: Also revokes every active ShareLink on this card — recipients get a 410, not a silently-still-working link.

post.description: JPEG, PNG, or WebP, up to 20 MB. Replacing an existing logo deletes the old one from storage.
post.summary: Upload or replace this card’s logo

post.description: JPEG, PNG, or WebP, up to 5 MB. Replacing an existing cover deletes the old one from storage. The image is stored and served exactly as sent — the client is expected to have already cropped it to the card's aperture (1:0.7). No server-side re-crop, re-fit, or re-compress happens.
post.summary: Upload or replace this card’s cover photo

delete.description: Same effect as PATCH /cards/:id with { "coverUrl": null } — either works.

put.description: All-or-nothing: every fieldId must be one of your own, non-archived, non-PHOTO ProfileFields, or nothing changes. This REPLACES the whole set — send everything you want kept, not just what changed.
put.summary: Replace this card’s curated field set

post.description: Mints (or reuses — see architecture invariant #1) the ShareLink for this (card, contact) pair and enqueues a WhatsApp send via the outbox. The send only actually goes out once a CARD_SHARE WhatsAppTemplate is registered and approved (POST /templates) — until then it fails cleanly with CARD_SHARE_TEMPLATE_NOT_CONFIGURED, but the returned url is real and live regardless, so copying it manually always works. Calling this again on an already-active link is a no-op on the messaging side — nothing re-sends.
post.summary: Share this card with a contact

get.description: Active ShareLinks only — a revoked or never-shared contact has no link to notify. versionsBehind is currentVersion minus the version each recipient was last told about, via either the initial share or a previous notify.
get.summary: List active recipients and how far behind each one is

post.description: The message carries no field-level diff — just a pointer at the live link. Each shareLinkId must be an ACTIVE link on this card. Fails cleanly with CARD_UPDATE_TEMPLATE_NOT_CONFIGURED until a CARD_UPDATE WhatsAppTemplate is registered and approved (POST /templates). Re-notifying the same recipient about a version already notified is a no-op, not a duplicate send.
post.summary: Send a generic "this card was updated" WhatsApp notice to chosen recipients

get.summary: List every share link across all your cards

patch.description: Restoring reuses the same token — see POST /cards/:id/share for why a link is never re-minted.
patch.summary: Revoke or restore a share link

post.description: Records a template that already exists in Twilio — this does not create anything in Twilio itself. Create the template in Twilio Console/Content API first, submit it for WhatsApp approval, then register its contentSid here.

patch.description: Nothing here checks Twilio for you — set approvalStatus after confirming in Twilio Console. The (currently unbuilt) reconciler cron will do this automatically later.
patch.summary: Update a template’s approval status or active flag

get.description: One row per (fromPhoneE164, toPhoneE164) pair, ever — a real WhatsApp message, a QR-scan "Save & connect", and an owner-initiated card share all land here, distinguished by `source`. A second event of the same kind between a pair already on file produces no new row. No ownership scoping (`resolvedOwnerId` narrows QR_SCAN_CONNECT/CARD_SHARE rows, but this endpoint itself returns everyone's). Newest first, capped at 500 rows per call.

parameters.name: fromPhoneE164
parameters.description: Only rows from this phone number.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Only rows of this kind — a real message, a QR-scan connect, or a card share.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Max rows to return, newest first.

get.summary: History of inbound WhatsApp messages and connection events

get.description: Replaces the client-side assembly of GET /cards + GET /contacts + GET /share-links + one GET /cards/:id/audience per card (an N+1 on every load). Every count here is computed from the caller's own non-archived cards and their ACTIVE ShareLinks only — see DashboardResponseDto for the exact contract each field follows.
get.summary: Everything the dashboard screen needs, in one call

post.description: JPEG, PNG, or WebP, up to 20 MB. Stored as a WORK-category field so it carries over to any card that includes your work fields. Replacing an existing logo deletes the old one from storage.
post.summary: Upload or replace your profile-level company logo

info.title: ContactBook API
info.description: Every error response uses one envelope: {statusCode, code, message, requestId, details?}. Branch on `code`, not on `message` — see docs/architecture/lld.md §3.

cookie.name: cb_access_token
cookie.description: Set automatically by POST /auth/otp/verify. This is how the browser dashboard authenticates.

devCode.description: Present ONLY outside production, and only when Twilio is not configured. Lets the whole login flow be tested before real credentials exist. Never sent otherwise, never logged.

code.description: Stable, machine-readable — branch on this, not on `message`.

requestId.description: Matches the X-Request-Id response header — hand this to support to find the exact log line.

accessToken.description: Same token as the cb_access_token cookie, returned here too so non-browser clients (mobile apps, scripts, Postman) can use it directly as an Authorization: Bearer header instead of relying on cookies. 15-minute lifetime. The refresh token is deliberately NOT included here — it is long-lived (30 days) and stays httpOnly-cookie-only to limit its exposure to XSS; only the short-lived access token trades that protection for portability.

isOnboardingCompleted.description: Whether POST /profile/onboarding has been completed. false → new user, redirect to onboarding; true → returning user, proceed to the app.

accessToken.description: A freshly issued access token — see VerifyOtpResponseDto for why only this one is returned.

primaryPhone.description: The OTP-verified phone — never independently editable.

value.description: Always the plaintext value — decrypted server-side for financial types before this response is built. Never logged: see common/logging/redact.ts.

groupId.description: Set when this field belongs to one instance of a repeatable thing (a specific job, bank account, etc).

financial.description: Bank accounts, digital wallets, and crypto wallets — all category FINANCIAL, distinguished by which FieldTypes their fields use.

accountNumber.description: Encrypted at rest automatically — see field-encryption.util.ts.

financial.description: Bank accounts, digital wallets, and crypto wallets — all category FINANCIAL, distinguished by which FieldTypes their fields use.

type.description: PHOTO cannot be created here — use POST /profile/photo instead.

position.description: Defaults to last position if omitted.

groupId.description: Attaches this field to one instance of a repeatable thing (a specific job, bank account, etc). Must belong to you — the id of a group belonging to another user is rejected, not silently ignored. Omit for a "loose" field like a personal phone number.

position.description: Defaults to last position if omitted.

orderedIds.description: Field ids in the new display order. Every id must belong to the caller — ids belonging to another user are rejected, not silently skipped.

optedOutAt.description: Set when this contact has texted STOP. Blocks future sends; existing links stay live.

notes.description: Private to you — never shown to the contact.

displayName.description: Whatever the imported source (device address book, CSV, ...) called them.

contacts.description: Typically the caller’s device address book, handed over however the client sourced it — this endpoint doesn’t care whether that was a native Contacts API, a CSV, or a manual multi-add.

created.description: Phone numbers that were not already in your registry.

updated.description: Phone numbers already in your registry — displayName was refreshed from the import if provided.

label.description: labelOverride if set on this card, otherwise the field’s own label.

value.description: Decrypted plaintext for financial types, same as the field editor — this is your own view of what you are about to share.

publicUrl.description: This card’s own public URL — what its QR code encodes. Independent of any recipient: it exists before the card has ever been shared with anyone, and revoking one recipient’s link never affects it. Resolves through the same public endpoint as a per-recipient share link.

logoUrl.description: Set only via POST /cards/:id/logo — never accepted on create/update. NULL until the owner uploads one.

coverUrl.description: Set only via POST /cards/:id/cover — never a raw string on create/update (PATCH accepts only an explicit `null` to remove it). Already cropped by the client to the card's aperture; served verbatim, never re-cropped server-side. NULL until the owner uploads one.

headline.description: Printed under the name — overrides the profile job title on this card. NULL means not set.

templateId.description: Never null — defaults to "meridian" when never chosen.

finish.description: Defaults to "gradient" when never chosen; still nullable via PATCH.

texture.description: Defaults to "none" when never chosen; still nullable via PATCH.

templateId.description: Not nullable — every card always has a template.

paletteId.description: null clears it (falls back to the template default).

groundHex.description: Free colour, #RRGGBB. Overrides paletteId when set. null clears it.

finish.description: null clears it (falls back to the "gradient" default).

texture.description: null clears it (falls back to the "none" default).

headline.description: Printed under the name — overrides the profile job title on this card. null clears it.

coverUrl.description: The ONLY accepted value is literal null, to remove the cover — same effect as DELETE /cards/:id/cover. A real cover can only ever be set by uploading one via POST /cards/:id/cover, never as a string here.

fieldId.description: Must be one of your own ProfileField ids — a field belonging to another user is rejected, not silently skipped.

visible.description: Soft-hide without losing this field’s position or label override.

labelOverride.description: Shown instead of the field’s own label, on this card only.

fields.description: The full curated set, in display order — this REPLACES whatever the card currently has, it does not merge.

contactId.description: Must be one of your own Contact ids — add it first via POST /contacts or POST /contacts/import. A contact belonging to another user is rejected, not silently ignored.

url.description: What actually goes in the WhatsApp message. Resolves live — never a snapshot.

lastNotifiedVersion.description: The card version this recipient was last told about, via share or notify. Null only for a link that predates this feature and has never been notified since.

versionsBehind.description: card.currentVersion minus lastNotifiedVersion — 0 means fully caught up.

recipients.description: Active ShareLinks only — a revoked or never-shared contact has no link to notify.

shareLinkIds.description: ShareLink ids to notify — from GET /cards/:id/audience. Each must be an ACTIVE link on this card; anything else is rejected, not silently skipped.

status.description: The send is queued, not confirmed delivered — it fails cleanly with CARD_UPDATE_TEMPLATE_NOT_CONFIGURED until a CARD_UPDATE WhatsAppTemplate is approved.
REVOKED immediately 410s the public link. Setting ACTIVE again restores the same token — it is never regenerated.

bodyPreview.example: Hi! {{1}} shared their ContactBook card with you. Tap below to view their latest contact details.

key.description: Your own semantic name — what the app looks up templates by, not Twilio’s id.

contentSid.description: The ContentSid Twilio assigned when this template was created in Content API / Console.

bodyPreview.example: Hi! {{1}} shared their ContactBook card with you. Tap below to view their latest contact details.
bodyPreview.description: Mirror of the approved body text, for humans reading the registry — not sent to Twilio.

variableSchema.description: Documents what each numbered Twilio variable means, in the order the template body/button use them. Not validated against Twilio — this is our own record for whoever builds the send call.

approvalStatus.description: Set this to APPROVED only after confirming in Twilio Console — nothing here checks Twilio for you yet.
Set after checking Twilio Console — nothing here verifies against Twilio yet.

isActive.description: Flip off to stop this template from being picked for new sends without deleting the registry row.

source.description: WHATSAPP_MESSAGE = a real inbound WhatsApp webhook hit. QR_SCAN_CONNECT = a stranger scanned a card QR and verified their phone via the public "Save & connect" flow. CARD_SHARE = an owner shared a card with a contact. Neither of the latter two involves an actual WhatsApp message Twilio delivered to us.

providerMessageId.description: Twilio MessageSid. Null for QR_SCAN_CONNECT rows.

fromPhoneE164.description: Whoever initiated contact — the message sender, the QR scanner, or the card owner (for a CARD_SHARE row).

toPhoneE164.description: For WHATSAPP_MESSAGE, our fixed WhatsApp business number. For QR_SCAN_CONNECT, the phone number of the card owner who was scanned. For CARD_SHARE, the phone number of the contact the card was shared with.

profileName.description: WhatsApp's own display name for the sender, if provided.

resolvedOwnerId.description: The ContactBook User this row resolves to, if any. Always set for QR_SCAN_CONNECT and CARD_SHARE (both know exactly which owner this is about). Always null for WHATSAPP_MESSAGE today — no scan-code-in-message resolution exists yet.

peopleReached.description: DISTINCT contacts holding at least one ACTIVE ShareLink — not the contact count, and not the link count. One person holding three cards is one person.

peopleOpened.description: DISTINCT contacts who have opened at least one ACTIVE link. The people-shaped counterpart to neverOpened, which counts LINKS — one person may hold three links and have opened only one, so neither is derivable from the other. Computed from the same single pass as peopleReached, so it can never exceed it.

totalOpens.description: viewCount summed over ACTIVE links only — a revoked link’s opens are history.

behind.description: DISTINCT contacts behind on at least one ACTIVE card — always a subset of, never greater than, peopleReached. null (never 0) when there is nothing to compute this from — e.g. no cards yet. Rendered differently on purpose: "we don't know" is not the same claim as "nobody is behind."

opens.description: Summed viewCount across this card’s ACTIVE links.

count.description: Meaning depends on kind: recipients behind (behind), recipients who never opened (never-opened), or 0 as a fixed marker for the binary kinds (no-fields, never-shared).

ShareLinks CREATED in this week, across all this owner’s cards, regardless of current status. This measures link creation, not opens — see the card-appearance spec §4.3 for why an opens-over-time chart doesn’t exist yet.

name.description: The group’s own tag, or a title-cased fallback of its category when untagged.

fieldCount.description: Non-archived fields in this group. Empty groups are included, not filtered out.

cardReach.description: One row per non-archived card, including cards with zero opens/recipients.

attention.description: Grouped by kind in priority order (no-fields, behind, never-opened, never-shared), worst (highest count) first within each kind.

sharingActivity.description: 12 weekly buckets, oldest first, ending with the current week.

groups.description: Every non-archived group, including empty ones.
